details:
Project Details: Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer

NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026

Our project is an interactive learning platform designed to give young students a virtual astronaut training experience.

1. What does it do or how does it work?

It simulates astronaut training through interactive space missions, planet exploration, quizzes, and mission-based challenges. Students learn basic space science while completing virtual astronaut tasks.

2. What are its benefits?

  • Makes space education fun and interactive.
  • Improves scientific knowledge and problem-solving skills.
  • Encourages teamwork and creativity.
  • Makes astronaut training concepts accessible to young learners.

3. What is the intended impact?

To inspire the next generation of space explorers and develop curiosity about science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM).

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

We plan to use:

  • HTML and CSS for the user interface.
  • JavaScript for interactive missions and game logic.
  • Visual Studio Code for development.
  • NASA open-source data and educational resources for scientific accuracy.

The project can be developed as a web application without additional hardware.

5. How is your project creative?

It combines space science with game-based learning. Students become virtual mission commanders and make decisions that affect the survival and success of their Moon or Mars outpost.

6. What factors did your team consider?

  • Age and understanding level of students.
  • Limited energy and food resources.
  • Oxygen and life-support requirements.
  • Radiation protection.
  • User-friendly design and educational value.

Important: NASA's actual challenge focuses on managing a lunar or Martian outpost and balancing these resources, rather than simply completing astronaut quizzes.
